MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Diagnostic testing for Fragile X syndrome

TEST PERFORMED
FMR1 and FMR2 Gene Expansion Analysis by PCR

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from peripheral blood. PCR amplification with fluorescent primers was performed to detect CGG repeat expansions in the FMR1 gene (FRAXA locus) and GCC repeat expansions in the FMR2 gene (FRAXE locus). Fragment analysis was performed by capillary electrophoresis. This assay detects repeat expansions but does not detect point mutations, deletions, or other rearrangements.

RESULTS

FMR1 (FRAXA) Analysis:
Allele 1: 30 CGG repeats - NORMAL
Allele 2: 31 CGG repeats - NORMAL

FMR2 (FRAXE) Analysis:
Allele 1: 12 GCC repeats - NORMAL
Allele 2: 15 GCC repeats - NORMAL

Repeat Range Classifications:
FRAXA (FMR1):
- Normal: 6-50 CGG repeats
- Intermediate: 51-60 CGG repeats
- Premutation: 61-200 CGG repeats
- Full mutation: >200 CGG repeats

FRAXE (FMR2):
- Normal: 6-30 GCC repeats
- Intermediate: 31-60 GCC repeats
- Premutation: 61-200 GCC repeats
- Full mutation: >200 GCC repeats

INTERPRETATION
No expansion mutations detected in FMR1 or FMR2 genes. Both FRAXA and FRAXE results are within the normal range. These results significantly reduce the likelihood of Fragile X syndrome to less than 1%.

TEST LIMITATIONS
This PCR-based assay is designed to detect CGG and GCC repeat expansions only. A small percentage of Fragile X syndrome cases may result from point mutations, deletions, or other rearrangements in the FMR1 gene that are not detected by this method. If clinical suspicion remains high, additional testing such as FMR1 gene sequencing or deletion/duplication analysis may be considered.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
